newsitem.title: ITALY: Mobutu resignation would not solve crisis-UN chief.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu resignation would not solve crisis-UN chief.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Tuesday that any decision by President Mobutu Sese Seko to resign would not in itself solve Zaire's crisis and he urged all sides in the Central African nation to negotiate peaceful change.
"We are facing a situation now where some have asked Mobutu to leave but that will not in itself solve the problem," Annan told a news conference at the end of a visit to Italy.
"And if you were to march into Kinshasa that is not a solution either," he said.

Zaire's ailing president has rejected rebel demands for him to quit and has said he had no plans to go into exile. But the veteran president has not ruled out direct talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

Annan said all sides in the conflict in Zaire would to have a part in managing a change towards democratic transition and elections "otherwise we will create vacuums and chaotic situations that will be extremely difficult to manage".
He added: "Unless we get hold of this at early stage and get them to discuss it, we may risk losing contol of it".
Annan has appealed to U.N. members to press Kabila to accept a ceasefire and a negotiated solution to his country's crisis.
"I hope he (Kabila) will respond because the statements he has made so far (say) that he is for a united Zaire," Annan said.

"He's not out to break up Zaire, he's not out for secession. What he wants is to see a democratically elected government. If that is indeed his intention then what the international community is proposing is a very viable option and a good route," Annan added.
Annan said it was incumbent on both sides to help implement a five-point peace plan endorsed by the Security Council.
Kabila's rebels now control half of the huge Central African nation including its mineral-rich economic heart. His forces captured Zaire's second city, Lubumbashi, last week.
U.S., French, Belgian and British troops are in neighbouring Congo to evacuate their nationals from Kinshasa if necessary.
